summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with septic shock due to MSSA bacteremia, likely originating from her tunneled hemodialysis catheter. She presented with fever, hypotension, and weakness. The infected catheter was removed, and she was started on vancomycin. Blood cultures confirmed MSSA, and a TEE ruled out endocarditis. She improved clinically with normalization of labs and resolution of fever. Renal function remained stable without need for dialysis during admission. Due to claustrophobia, she declined MRI to evaluate possible spinal hardware infection. IV antibiotic therapy will be completed at home via PICC line. Chronic pain management was transitioned away from narcotics due to prior contract violations and adverse reaction to tramadol. She was discharged home with home infusion services and close follow-up planned.
